learning: Tests whether mass drives bend overshoot once line loss is geometrically closed on the oval. If line_loss_events stays at 1 on the S-bend or slalom, the loss is not geometric, and the line_loss handling and start position should be checked before further geometry changes.
notes: Complete robot on the 0.6 kg mass test: iteration 3 array and controller, with mass the only geometry change. Keeping the controller fixed isolates whether lower yaw inertia reduces S-bend and slalom overshoot. The 0.6 kg reduction is the single variable.
rationale: Iteration 3 is the only design with the +/-0.05 m array, and its evidence is mixed. Line loss fell to 0 on the oval (from 1 to 2 events on earlier designs), but the S-bend and slalom still logged one loss each, and every run ended off_track with max_error about 0.064 m. Progress stayed at 0.11 to 0.17, so runs are lost early. Iteration 1 showed that kp 3.0 raised steering_oscillation to 0.186 and max_error to 0.068 m, so gains stay at the damped iteration 2/3 set (kp 2.5, kd 0.2, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.3). The Builder's intent is to test whether reducing mass from 0.7 kg to 0.6 kg lowers yaw inertia and bend overshoot. To isolate that effect, I keep the geometry fixed apart from mass: same 16 mm footprints, same +/-0.05 m positions at y = 0.04 m, same wheel_track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body_width 0.12 m and body_length 0.18 m. The controller is also unchanged, including the outer-scaled sensor weights [-1.5, -1.05, -0.6, 0, 0.6, 1.05, 1.5], which keep the signal monotonic over the span. The last_direction line-loss handling stays unchanged, so any remaining S-bend or slalom loss can be attributed to the controller or start position rather than to this change. Expected result: if mass is the lever, max_error falls below 0.06 m and progress rises above iteration 3. If line loss persists at 1 on the S-bend or slalom, the feedback's decision triggers point to the controller side. I cannot predict the outcome, and this package has not yet raced.
